podcasts.title: The One-Person Biotech | OpenAI Life Sciences
podcasts.description:
What happens when scientists are no longer limited by human attention? OpenAI’s Joy Jiao and Ashoka Rajendra join a16z’s Jay Rughani and Jorge Conde to discuss how AI and thousands of parallel agents could reshape drug discovery and development.

They trace OpenAI’s life sciences work from scientific reasoning to the acquisition of Orchestra Bio, and how agents could search biological data, manage clinical trials, and navigate regulatory and manufacturing workflows.

They also discuss AI’s role in solving difficult diagnoses and a future where a single person could potentially launch and advance multiple biotech programs.

podcasts.title: Replay: How the Internet Happened | Chris Dixon & Brian McCullough (2018)
podcasts.description:
Why do technologies that look like bad ideas in one era become enormous companies in the next? Originally recorded in 2018, Brian McCullough and Chris Dixon trace the companies, failures, and accidents that built the modern internet.

They revisit the battle between the open web and more centralized visions of the “information superhighway,” why eBay helped establish trust between strangers online, what Napster understood about digital media, and how Google found a business model for search.

They also look at the dot-com crash and the ideas that arrived before the technology was ready, from cloud storage to grocery delivery, asking what those cycles can teach founders about spotting the next wave.

podcasts.title: The Professional Network Built for You and Your AI Agent
podcasts.description:
What if your AI agent could find the people you should know before you even start looking? Cosign is building a professional network around reputation and trusted recommendations, and now agents can use that network too.

MTS host Sophia Dew sits down with a16z’s David Booth and Cosign’s Bella Nazzari to discuss what they’ve learned since launching Cosign, why traditional profiles often miss the operators doing the most important work, and how the Cosign Awards are surfacing talent through the people willing to vouch for them.

They also explore an emerging behavior: people connecting their agents to Cosign to continuously find relevant people, lists, and opportunities, and what professional networking could look like when both humans and their agents participate.
